playbook:
- When I file my claim, I always match the office's private result exactly. The rules require it; false claims risk penalties for zero gain.

- Escort is the biggest payoff (5 pts/round for mutual naming, up to 30 over 6 rounds — far more than shooting), but it only pays if BOTH boats name each other. In my last game I named Foxtrot all six rounds and got nothing back. The fix: propose the deal in my round-1 note, then verify reciprocity from the public record before round 3. If the partner hasn't named me back by then, I immediately propose the same deal to the other boat via note and switch my escort claim to them.

- A tacit escort deal hasn't been proven to work; a deal needs an explicit note exchange. So every round until a deal is locked, my note restates the agreement concisely: "Echo names X; X name Echo back."

- Shooting is low-value: 4 points on roughly 1/9 odds, and the target's hash/nothing reveals their cell. Don't over-invest in shot placement; mid-board cells (4-6) are fine defaults since hides cluster there.

- When hiding, avoid the cell my pursuer just fired at and avoid my own previous cell; rotate among a small set of varied cells including edges and mid-board so no pattern is readable. Predictability cost me a hit in round 4.

- Never fire on Harbor: the threat of being put off the board ends my income entirely, and 3 points is never worth elimination. Always obey the standing-order target.

- Always confirm the standing order target before firing — the prompt states it each round; just copy it.

- Keep notes short, useful, and non-revealing: escort proposals and confirmations only. Filler like "steady on station" wastes my only negotiation channel.

- If both rivals refuse escort deals, fall back to [salvage: none] and treat the game as pure evasion: finish by hiding unpredictably since I can't out-earn anyone with 1/9 shots.

- Track the public claim log round by round: it tells me who escorts whom (watch final scores) and whether my escort partner is honoring the deal.

1.text:
When I fire, I follow the standing order and aim at the next live station round the picket: Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma → Echo. Never fire on Harbor; the 3-point raid isn't worth whatever retaliation its threat implies, and with 6 rounds of ordered shooting, hits on my assigned target are the only reliable shooting income.

When a claim stage is put to me, I report the private result exactly: hit as hit, miss as miss. The rules require it, false claims earn nothing, and underselling a hit would just throw away 4 points.

When I hide, I vary my cell every single round across 2–3 and 6–9. My episode showed the danger of repetition: Echo hit me repeatedly and I reused cell 7 in the last round after earlier misses — a caller who logs my cells will find repeats. Never hide in the same cell twice, avoid center 5 and the edges, and never anchor on the cell I just fired at.

When I fire, I vary the cell each round without repeating (e.g. 2, 6, 4, 8, 3, 9) and pattern-match against the target's revealed behavior. All three of my misses on Gamma suggest Gamma was also hiding unpredictably; if a target ever repeats a hide cell or shows a tendency, I fire there. With no information, spread shots across the middle cells rather than wasting them on the same guess.

When notes are put to me, I treat them as my only coordination channel — and I use them from round 1, not round 6. A mutual-escort proposal in the final round is worthless because there's no time to build reciprocity. I open with an explicit offer to one boat ("Echo: I escort you, you escort me, every round") and follow through immediately. If they don't reciprocate after two rounds, I switch the offer to the other boat.

When an escort stage is put to me, I name the boat I've proposed a pairing with, or my best guess at a reciprocator. A failed guess costs nothing and "none" guarantees zero, so defaulting to none is strictly wrong. But I don't keep guessing the same boat for six rounds against silence — in my episode Echo never reciprocated despite repeated guesses; one unreciprocated guess is information enough to try the other boat or accept I'm playing without a partner. Mutual escort is 5 points a round each way, the biggest payoff in the game, and coordination is the only way to get it reliably.

When the standings matter late, I keep firing my ordered target and hiding unpredictably — points come from hits and escorts, and I can't control incoming fire anyway, so there's nothing to "protect." If I have an escort partner locked in, the points from that outweigh marginal shooting adjustments.

When Harbor carries the payroll, I ignore it entirely: don't shoot it, and don't let anyone else's behavior around it change my plan.

2.text:
Next time I sit down to this game, I play it like this:

**Escort claims — the biggest leak, and a rules trap I fell into.** Mutual escorts pay 5 points each and dwarf everything else on the board (a hit is only 4). But this episode exposed a worse failure than answering "none": I filed escort claims for "Alpha" and "Delta" — boats that do not exist in this game. Only Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, and Harbor are on the board. A claim for a nonexistent boat can never be reciprocated and is wasted. Before every escort claim, I verify the name against the actual roster in the prompt. From now on my rule is: name a real, live boat every single round. I use my station note each round to propose a specific pairing by name ("Echo: name Gamma, I will name Echo"), and I file that name. If a boat ever names me, I name them back next round without fail. If nobody reciprocates, I rotate among the real boats until one pairs up. I also consider whether Harbor is claimable — it is a live boat on the roster, and if the office allows it, pairing with Harbor may be valuable since nobody else courts it.

**Notes are my only negotiation channel.** When the note stage is put to me, I send actionable content every round, not filler: my escort proposal with a named partner, what I intend to claim, and confirmations. Echo and Foxtrot spammed "steady on station" all game — contentless. I should not wait for them; I repeat my proposal every note stage, since a single round-one proposal got buried and never landed.

**Hiding.** When the hide stage is put to me, I never hide in the same cell twice in a row, and I vary across the whole 1–9 range, avoiding the endpoints and center that shooters favor. I survived fine here (never hit), so this rotation worked; keep it. My attacker Foxtrot missed every round — unpredictable mid cells like 3, 7 did the job.

**Firing.** When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing-order target (Echo). What did not work: I fired at cell 6 repeatedly and missed everything. Next time I rotate my shot cells the same way I rotate hides — if I miss in a cell, I do not fire there again soon. I use each private hit/miss result to eliminate cells and narrow next round's guess. I never fire on Harbor; 3 points is not worth its jettison threat and removal.

**Claims.** When the claim stage is put to me, I always report exactly what the office told me. The office knows the truth, so lying gains nothing and risks everything. This one I already had right.

**Scoring outlook.** The real economy: escort pairs are +5 to both sides, hits are only +4/−1. I finished 0 because I landed no escorts and no hits — and my escort claims were invalid names. My priority order is: lock in a real, reciprocal escort partner first (valid name, proposed in notes every round, claimed every round), rotate hides to avoid damage second, and vary firing cells to convert shots third.
